editorial.description_en: A wet whetstone: a cool mid grey with the chroma pulled almost to nothing.
editorial.description_ja: 水にぬらした砥石のような、しずかな灰色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.640, C 0.009, h 250.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 研ぎ (togi, sharpening) + 石 (ishi, stone). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Whetstone" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 研石. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — suzu-gami at ΔE00 7.5, hai-suna at ΔE00 8.2, sawa-ishi at ΔE00 9.4. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.009 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
